title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 162 (Appointment of directors to be voted individually)

content.overview: Section 162 provides that at a general meeting a motion for the appointment of two or more persons as directors of the company by a single resolution shall not be moved unless a resolution that it shall be so moved has first been agreed to by the meeting without any vote being given against it. A resolution moved in contravention is void, whether or not objection was taken at the time.
content.glance: Two or more directors cannot be appointed by one resolution unless the meeting first agrees without any dissenting vote that a single resolution may be used; a contravening resolution is void.
content.study: At a general meeting of a company, a motion for the appointment of two or more persons as directors of the company by a single resolution shall not be moved unless a resolution that it shall be so moved has first been agreed to by the meeting without any vote being given against it. A resolution moved in contravention of this provision is void, whether or not its being so moved was objected to at the time. Nothing in the section applies to a company whose articles provide for election of directors by proportional representation under section 163. Current-law framing: identify a multi-person appointment motion at a general meeting; check whether a prior unanimous-consent resolution authorised a single resolution; if not, the appointment resolution is void.

sections.heading: Default Rule
sections.body: Directors are to be voted on individually at a general meeting; a single resolution for two or more persons is not the default.

sections.heading: Exception
sections.body: A single resolution may be used only if the meeting first agrees, without any vote against, that it shall be so moved.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.body: A resolution moved in contravention is void, whether or not objection was taken at the time.

sections.heading: Proportional Representation Carve-Out
sections.body: The section does not apply where articles provide for election by proportional representation under section 163.

provisions.title: Appointment of directors to be voted individually

examples.title: Slate vote without prior consent
examples.body: The chair moves one resolution appointing A, B and C as directors without a prior resolution agreeing that a single motion may be used. Under s. 162 the resolution is void.

examples.title: Prior consent obtained
examples.body: The meeting first passes, without any dissenting vote, a resolution that the appointment of three directors may be moved by a single resolution. The subsequent single resolution is then within s. 162.

hypotheticals.question: Does failure to object at the meeting save a multi-person appointment resolution moved without prior consent?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 162 states that a resolution moved in contravention is void whether or not its being so moved was objected to at the time.

distinctions.title: Individual voting (s. 162) vs proportional representation (s. 163)
distinctions.left: Default individual voting; single resolution only with prior unanimous-consent resolution
distinctions.right: Articles may adopt proportional representation; s. 162 then does not apply

misconceptions.trap: A single resolution for several directors is always valid if no one objects at the meeting.
misconceptions.correction: Without a prior resolution agreed to without any vote against, a multi-person appointment resolution is void even if no one objected when it was moved.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 162 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify multi-person appointment motion at GM. II. Check prior unanimous-consent resolution. III. If absent, resolution is void. IV. Note s. 163 carve-out if applicable. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Meeting facts; motion structure; prior consent status; precise relief.

examTips: Single resolution needs prior consent with no dissenting vote.
Contravention → void even without contemporaneous objection.

enhancement.definition: Section 162 requires directors to be voted on individually at a general meeting unless the meeting first agrees without any dissenting vote that a single resolution may appoint two or more persons; a contravening resolution is void.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Members must be able to accept or reject each proposed director separately unless they unanimously permit a slate vote.
essentialIngredients: General meeting appointment of two or more persons
Prior resolution agreed without any vote against
Otherwise the appointment resolution is void
Does not apply where s. 163 proportional representation applies
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 162 protects members from forced slate appointments at general meetings.

keyTakeaways: Single resolution needs prior no-dissent consent.
